translation_notes: `ns = Namespace(ns_uri)` -> `@prefix ns: f<{ns_uri}> as NS .` (a computed IRI; the object stays because `g.bind(model.__name__.lower(), NS)` takes it by value under a prefix computed at run time, which no lexical @prefix can name). `URIRef(ns[x])` -> `ns:{x}` (ns[...] concatenates without encoding, like `ns:{expr}`). Two g.add in the loop and the three of the metadata block -> +{ } (the latter one island).

Typed literals: inside the metadata island `Literal(dump_name, datatype=XSD.string)` and `Literal(now.isoformat(), datatype=XSD.dateTime)` become `{dump_name}^^xsd:string` and `{...}^^xsd:dateTime`. In the field loop the literal is built in a five-branch chain and added once at the end: `{x}^^dt` exists only INSIDE an island (`literal = {v}^^xsd:integer` is a SyntaxError), so the branches keep Literal(field_value, datatype=xsd:T) (XSD.T -> prefixed name) and the final add is `+{ {s} {p} {literal} }`; using the typed island would mean five copies of the add, a refactoring.

Known gap: dump_name=None would write 'None' in the original (and in the file name) but raises TypeError with `{dump_name}^^xsd:string` in ldpy 0.7.1; dump_name is a documented str, and the driver does not test None.

Context shim (context_shim.py): `settings.BASE_DIR` = '.', Django not in the venv; `import logging` restored in original.py (the extracted header lacked it). The driver freezes datetime.now() for both sides, stands in for the Django model, and wraps Graph.serialize to print the exact N-Triples of the local graph to stdout: Turtle is lossy for an ill-typed literal ("true"^^xsd:integer is written bare), so the written file alone let a boolean-typed-as-integer mutant survive. A second phase compares the written Turtle text (prefix table). 9 mutants killed.
optimization_notes: optimized.py: the five-branch isinstance chain becomes a for/else over (type, datatype) pairs in the same order (bool before int), with the add in the loop and the warning in the else; Literal(dt.isoformat(), datatype=XSD.dateTime) becomes Literal(dt, datatype=XSD.dateTime), whose lexical form rdflib computes with the same isoformat(), so the datetime branch needs no special case; ns_uri, class_uri, field_name, predicate_uri, metadata_class, dump_metadata, target_dir and timestamp are inlined; URIRef(ns[x]) loses the redundant URIRef; the three metadata adds become one `g += [...]`; strftime becomes a format spec in the file-name f-string. The `with open(...)` is kept before serialize, so an unwritable directory still raises before the graph is serialised.

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: the namespace IRI expression goes straight into `@prefix ns: f<{...}> as NS .` (NS kept for g.bind under a computed prefix); `@graph g` after g = Graph(); the two loop adds and the metadata block become +{ } islands, the field literal `{field_value}^^{datatype}` with the datatype interpolated from the pair, which gives Literal(value, datatype=...) as before; `ns:{instance.pk}` needs no str() because the prefixed name builds its local part as a string.
Gap kept from the translation: dump_name=None writes "None" in the original but raises TypeError with `{dump_name}^^xsd:string`; dump_name is a documented str and the driver does not test None.

The driver's second phase compares the written Turtle text of translated.ldpy only; the same comparison was run by hand on the four optimized artefacts (four cases each, all identical to original.py).
header_optimization_notes: Python: URIRef goes; XSD is imported from rdflib with the rest (one import line instead of two).
LD Python: Literal, Namespace, RDF, URIRef and XSD go, only Graph stays from rdflib; the xsd @prefix is used and stays.
